items.q: Do you only work with businesses in New York?
items.a: No. We are based in New York and give priority to New York City and Long Island, where we can also meet in person. We work remotely with businesses anywhere in the United States.

Small-business plans start at $149 a month for a website with Google Business Profile care. Custom software is priced after a short discovery and usually starts at a few thousand dollars. You always receive the price in writing before work starts.

items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: A small-business website usually goes live within a few weeks. Automations often take two to four weeks; web and mobile applications one to four months, depending on features.

items.q: Do I have to talk to you on the phone?
items.a: No. Everything can be handled in writing: by e-mail, text message, chat or our contact form. If you prefer to call, Ava, our AI phone assistant, answers 24/7 and we follow up in writing.

items.q: Who owns my website, my Google profile and my code?

about.title: Who we are
text: Zerone International LLC is a technology company based in Farmingville, New York, on Long Island. We help businesses get found online, answer every customer and replace manual work with reliable software.

We start close to home, in New York City and on Long Island, and work remotely with businesses in every state. We run our own company on the same tools we build for clients: an AI assistant answers our phone line, automations prepare our proposals, and every agreement is made in writing.
Alongside client work, we build our own software products, starting with tools for online sellers.

founder.title: Meet the founder
bio: Berk Divaroren founded Zerone International to give small and growing businesses the kind of technology that large companies take for granted: a website that brings in customers, a phone that is always answered, and software that does the repetitive work.

He started his first company, a computer software and hardware business in Adana, Turkey, in 2019. He holds a bachelor's degree in International Trade and Logistics from Anadolu University and moved to New York in January 2022, where he continued his studies in computer applications, business and management at the New York Institute of Finance.

Before founding Zerone International, he gained hands-on experience in online commerce on major US marketplaces. Today he leads the design of the company's own systems, from its AI phone assistant and automated written proposals to this website in 15 languages, and works directly with every client.

paragraphs: When you submit a form, it is sent to our form provider Formspree, which may use technically necessary cookies for spam protection. If we enable website statistics, we use a cookie-free service.

cases.title: A website for a home services company
cases.summary: A mobile-friendly website that turns local searches into calls and quote requests.
cases.challenge: Customers compare a few companies on their phone and call the one they trust.
cases.approach: A fast website with your services, service areas, real photos and reviews, one-tap call and quote buttons, and an accurate Google Business Profile behind it.

cases.title: Google Business Profile clean-up
cases.summary: Fix hours, categories, services and photos so the right customers find you on Google Maps.
cases.challenge: Wrong hours, a vague category or old photos send customers to a competitor.
cases.approach: We review the profile against Google's guidelines, correct every field, add services and photos, and set up a simple routine that keeps it current.

cases.title: Review requests after every job
cases.summary: A polite request with a direct link goes to every customer once the work is done.
cases.challenge: Happy customers rarely leave a review on their own, and asking by hand is easy to forget.
cases.approach: After each completed job, a short request goes out by e-mail or text, following Google's rules, and reply drafts for every new review wait for your approval.
includes: No rewards, no filtering of customers

cases.title: Local SEO for several locations
cases.summary: Consistent pages and listings for a business with several locations.
cases.challenge: Different details across directories confuse customers and search engines alike.
cases.approach: One page per location with structured data, the same business details across the main directories, and a report with calls and requests per location.

cases.title: AI receptionist for a professional office
cases.summary: Answer every call, share opening hours and take appointment requests, even after hours.
cases.challenge: Front-desk staff can't answer every call while helping clients in person.
cases.approach: An AI assistant answers when the line is busy or the office is closed, says that it is an AI, answers common questions and sends each request to the team in writing.

cases.title: After-hours calls for contractors
cases.summary: Capture the jobs that come in at night and on weekends.
cases.challenge: Contractors can't answer while they work, and evening callers simply call the next company.
cases.approach: The assistant answers, asks the questions you choose, such as address, problem and urgency, and texts you the urgent ones right away.

cases.title: Phone calls for a restaurant
cases.summary: Answer questions about hours, the menu and reservations during the dinner rush.
cases.challenge: The phone rings most when the kitchen is busiest, and unanswered calls cost tables.
cases.approach: The assistant answers common questions, takes reservation requests and passes everything else to the staff, with a written note for each call.
includes: Answers on hours, menu and directions

cases.title: Call summaries and written follow-up
cases.summary: Every call becomes a short written summary and, where useful, a draft follow-up e-mail.
cases.challenge: Details from phone calls get lost, and following up in writing takes time.
cases.approach: After each call, a summary with the caller's needs and contact details reaches you, and a follow-up draft is prepared for your approval.
includes: A written summary of each call
Nothing is sent without your approval

cases.title: Quotes and invoices from one form
cases.summary: Turn a customer request into a quote, and an accepted quote into an invoice.
cases.challenge: Typing the same customer details into several tools wastes time and causes mistakes.
cases.approach: A form or an e-mail starts the flow: the details become a quote draft, and once the customer accepts, an invoice with a hosted payment link.
includes: No card data on your systems

cases.title: Lead routing and instant alerts
cases.summary: Send every new inquiry to the right person within seconds, by e-mail, chat or text.
cases.challenge: Inquiries arrive by website, e-mail and social media, and some wait days for a reply.
cases.approach: All inquiries flow into one place, are sorted by type and area, and the right person gets an alert with a reply template.
includes: Alerts by e-mail, chat or text

cases.title: Appointment reminders
cases.summary: Automatic reminders and confirmations that reduce no-shows.
cases.challenge: Missed appointments cost time and money, and calling everyone the day before is not realistic.
cases.approach: Reminders go out at the times you choose, customers confirm or reschedule with one click, and your calendar updates itself.

cases.title: Weekly business reports
cases.summary: A plain-language report every Monday with the numbers you actually look at.
cases.challenge: Sales, calls, reviews and website visits live in different tools, so nobody looks at all of them.
cases.approach: A scheduled job collects the data, compares it with the previous week and sends a short report by e-mail or chat.
includes: Data from the tools you already use

cases.title: Customer portal
cases.summary: Let customers check status, documents and invoices without calling.
cases.challenge: Customers call to ask where things stand, and staff spend hours answering the same questions.
cases.approach: A secure portal shows each customer their own orders, documents and invoices, with a notification when something changes.

cases.title: Operations dashboard for owners
cases.summary: One screen with sales, jobs, calls and reviews, updated automatically.
cases.challenge: Owners piece the picture together from spreadsheets, e-mails and several apps.
cases.approach: A dashboard pulls the key numbers from your tools and shows the trends, with separate views for owners, managers and employees.

cases.title: Online booking system
cases.summary: Online booking with staff calendars, buffer times and confirmations.
cases.challenge: Bookings by phone and e-mail lead to double bookings and endless back-and-forth.
cases.approach: Customers pick a free time online, each staff member sees their own calendar, and confirmations and reminders go out automatically.

cases.title: From spreadsheets to a web app
cases.summary: Replace shared spreadsheets with one structured, secure workspace.
cases.challenge: Spreadsheets break when several people edit them, and nobody knows which version is right.
cases.approach: We turn the spreadsheet into a web application with forms, permissions, history and reports, and move your existing data over.

cases.title: Field service app
cases.summary: Jobs, addresses, checklists and photos in every technician's pocket.
cases.challenge: Technicians call the office for job details and fill in paper forms that get lost.
cases.approach: A mobile app shows each technician their jobs, checklists and customer notes, and sends photos and signatures back to the office.

cases.title: Inspection and site checklists
cases.summary: Digital checklists that work offline and produce a report on the spot.
cases.challenge: Paper checklists are hard to read, easy to lose and slow to turn into reports.
cases.approach: Inspectors fill in checklists on a phone or tablet, even without a connection, and a PDF report is created automatically.

cases.title: Loyalty and booking app
cases.summary: A branded app where regular customers book and collect rewards.
cases.challenge: Regular customers are the most valuable ones, but there is no simple way to stay in touch with them.
cases.approach: An iOS and Android app with booking, push notifications and a simple loyalty program, connected to your existing systems.

cases.title: Team tasks and time tracking
cases.summary: Assign tasks, track hours and see progress from any phone.
cases.challenge: Hours are written on paper and tasks are handed out by text, so nothing adds up at the end of the week.
cases.approach: Employees see their tasks and clock in and out in the app; managers see the progress and export hours for payroll.
